svg.aria-label: Exposed versus overlapped communication: interleaved NCCL hides behind compute, a lone all-reduce does not
svg.text: Exposed communication: what the trace shows
3% exposed: NCCL hides behind backward compute

g.text: gold: NCCL, interleaved: nothing the compute rows did not already cover

svg.text: 27% exposed: one lone all-reduce, nothing hides it

g.text: blue: compute finishes, then the full all-reduce sits alone on the timeline
gold block = exposed: GPUs communicate while compute rows sit empty

svg.text: The fix is overlap, not speed.
Smaller gradient buckets, larger microbatches, or an earlier comm start move
gold blocks under blue ones. Interleaved NCCL under backward = healthy; a lone
block with empty compute rows = exposed, and that is the number to kill.
